problem_text: A hemisphere with radius 200 sits on top of a horizontal circular disk with radius 200, and the hemisphere and disk have the same center. Let T be the region of points P in the disk such that a sphere of radius 42 can be placed on top of the disk at P and lie completely inside the hemisphere. The area of T divided by the area of the disk is p/q, where p and q are relatively prime positive integers. Find p+q.
notes: Hemisphere radius = disk radius = 200, small sphere radius = 42. Sphere sits on disk at horizontal dist d from center; internal tangency: sqrt(d^2+42^2) = 200-42=158  =>  d^2 = 158^2-42^2 = 200*116 = 23200. Ratio = 23200/40000 = 29/50. p+q = 79. Verified via Power of a Point (Solution 2) and coordinate geometry.
